resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection / Continued Certification of Occupancy (CCO) for resale
resale_co.issued_by: Vineland Fire Department, Fire Prevention Division
resale_co.lead_time: File as soon as a settlement date is set; at least 4 business days are needed, and filing more than 10 days before closing gets the lower fee
requirements: All construction permits closed before applying; unpermitted basement, garage or attic conversions are checked
No basement bedrooms without proper egress; zoning approval for duplex or triplex use; open Code Enforcement violations closed
Utilities on at the time of inspection
Exterior walls, gutters, foundation and accessory structures sound; yard free of trash, debris and abandoned vehicles
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting and readable from the street
Stairs, decks, porches and balconies sound; guardrails on landings or porches 30 inches high; handrails where there are 3 or more risers
No keyed deadbolts on the inside of exit doors; bedroom doors close and latch
In-ground pools fenced with self-closing, self-latching gates
Smoke alarm on each level and within 10 feet of sleeping areas; sealed battery units unless hardwired alarms already exist (hardwired must be kept)
Carbon monoxide alarm near bedrooms where there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Homes with a generator, solar or battery storage need a printed 'Caution Multiple Sources of Power' label at the electrical panel and meter box
No excessive peeling paint in pre-1978 homes; windows open and stay open with no broken glass; no holes in walls, ceilings or floors
Heater, water heater and chimney in working order; bathroom exhaust fan or window
Electrical free of hazards (covers on outlets and boxes, no open panel holes, no taped splices); an electrical certification may be required
Toilets flush without leaks, hot and cold water work, water heater bonding strap and relief valve pipe 2 to 6 inches off the floor

resale_co.how_to_apply: As soon as a settlement date is set, file the resale application in person at the Fire Administration building, 400 W. Plum St., Vineland (the application is in triplicate and must be completed in person; a watermarked sample is online). At least 4 business days are needed. Pay by check, cash or money order; fees are per unit and depend on how early you file. If the home fails, a new application and fee are needed before the reinspection. For vacant or uninhabitable homes the buyer can file a Certificate of Transfer of Title (CTT) affidavit together with the CCO application.

The applications are in triplicate form and need to be completed in person. A minimum of four (4) business days is required to complete process.
Check, cash, or money orders are accepted.

resale_co.notes: In Vineland the resale certificate and the smoke/CO certificate are one inspection by the Fire Department's Fire Prevention Division, called a Certificate of Inspection on the Selling Your Home page and a CCO (Continued Certification of Occupancy) on the application. It covers general housing items as well as smoke and CO alarms. Fees are per unit; the web page says 'more than 10 days' and '4 to 10 days' while the application (revised 07/2022) says '10 or more business days' and '4 to 10 business days'. The CTT (Certificate of Transfer of Title) is for homes sold vacant or uninhabitable: the buyer certifies the home will not be occupied until repairs are done and a CO is obtained from Licenses and Inspections, and the CTT application expires 90 days after it is received. Duplexes and multi-family buildings of 15 units or fewer should check with the Zoning Department before listing. The Selling Your Home page says to file at the Fire Administration building, 400 W. Plum St.; the Fire Marshal's page says the Fire Prevention Office is at the City Hall Annex, 625 E. Plum St. The phone given is the Fire Prevention office line from the City's department directory; the state directory lists (856) 794-4000 (City Hall main number) for Brian J Murray Sr.

Printed 'Caution Multiple Sources of Power' label at the electrical panel and meter box for homes with a generator, solar or battery storage
House numbers at least 4 inches high

fire_cert.notes: The Vineland Fire Department is the local fire enforcing agency (registry code F). Its Fire Prevention Division's resale CCO inspection includes the smoke and CO alarm check, so there is one application and one fee for both (the fees are listed under both sections but are paid once). The checklist (revised 02/2025) does not list a fire extinguisher; the June 2025 CTT page still has the buyer certify the home will get a fire extinguisher before occupancy. The 'Welcome from the Fire Marshall' page says the Fire Prevention Division inspects structures except owner-occupied dwellings on a regular basis; resale inspections are handled through the Selling Your Home process.

other_items.label: Open construction permits and unpermitted conversions
other_items.detail: All construction permits must be closed out before applying; basement, garage or attic conversions without permits are checked (Licenses and Inspections, 856-794-4113).

other_items.label: Zoning approval for duplex or multi-family use
other_items.detail: Duplex and multi-family (15 units or fewer) owners should contact the Zoning Department before listing to confirm the use is conforming (856-794-4113).

other_items.label: Open Code Enforcement violations
other_items.detail: Any open Code Enforcement violations must be closed out (856-794-3806).

other_items.label: Electrical certification
other_items.detail: An electrical certification may be required.
